Best practice for identifying and assessing the Dual-Use issues in enabling technologies research Executive Summary Research ethics and research integrity (RE&RI) are essential in performing advanced and competitive research and innovation in the field of programme the best practices focus on two basic pillars: fostering dissemination of du results between civilian and defence sectors and boosting networking of du oriented sme's with academic groups oriented to civilian research. establishing a higher authority to supervise sme ethical self- monitoring, with the mandate to impose sanctions; establishing joint training programmes for researchers in civilian and defence sectors to overcome existing differences in research culture that hamper cross-fertilization of knowledge and creation of an eventual du oriented european cluster/council. the full report is published on the eu bookshop studies and reports

metadata.title: Best Practice for Identifying and Assessing the Dual-Use Issues in Enabling Technologies Research (JANUS)
metadata.keywords: dual-use technology, enabling technologies, research policy

additional_metadata.General information about Best Practices: The JANUS project developed best practices to enhance synergies in dual-use research. It emphasises fostering dissemination between civilian and defence sectors and promoting networking between SMEs and academic groups. Recommendations include establishing joint training programs and creating a supervisory authority for ethical monitoring.
additional_metadata.Primary objective: To establish best practices for identifying and assessing dual-use issues in enabling technologies research.
additional_metadata.Secondary objective: To enhance collaboration between civilian and defence research sectors and promote ethical oversight in dual-use research.
additional_metadata.Implementation strategy:
The implementation strategy involves:

Engaging stakeholders through interviews and questionnaires.

Conducting case studies to identify practical challenges and solutions.

Developing guidelines and recommendations based on collected data.
additional_metadata.Success factors:
Active participation of stakeholders from both civilian and defence sectors.

Comprehensive analysis of existing literature and practices.

Development of practical and actionable recommendations.
additional_metadata.Challenges:
Bridging the cultural and operational differences between civilian and defence research communities.

Ensuring compliance with ethical standards across diverse organisations.

Navigating complex legal frameworks governing dual-use technologies.
additional_metadata.Alignment with EU Policies: The JANUS project aligns with the European Union's Horizon Europe framework and its emphasis on responsible research and innovation, particularly concerning dual-use technologies.
additional_metadata.Transferability: The best practices identified are applicable across various EU member states and can be adapted to different organisational contexts.
additional_metadata.Comment:

Strengths: Strong institutional collaboration, low-cost/high benefit simulation format, repeatability across contexts.
Minor Weakness: Not highly innovative in format, though conceptually tailored to new types of threats.
